title: 100 — Continue
content: The server received the request headers and the client should proceed to send the body. Used with the Expect: 100-continue header to avoid sending large bodies for nothing.
meaning: Keep going, everything is fine so far.

title: 101 — Switching Protocols
content: The client asked to switch protocols and the server agreed. This is what happens when an HTTP connection upgrades to WebSocket.
meaning: The connection is switching to a different protocol.

title: 102 — Processing
content: The server received the request and is still working on it, but there is no response yet. Keeps the client from assuming the connection dropped.
meaning: Still working on this, do not hang up yet.

title: 200 — OK
content: The request succeeded. On a GET the body carries the requested resource; on a POST it carries the result of the action.
meaning: Everything went fine.

title: 201 — Created
content: A new resource was created as a result of the request. The response usually includes a Location header pointing at the new resource.
meaning: Something new was created and here is where to find it.

title: 204 — No Content
content: The request succeeded but there is nothing to return in the body. Typical for a successful DELETE or a PUT that has no data to send back.
meaning: It worked, but there is nothing to show.

title: 301 — Moved Permanently
content: The resource moved to a new URL for good. Clients should update their links and use the new address from now on.
meaning: This moved for good, update your link.

title: 302 — Found
content: The resource is temporarily at a different URL. Unlike a 301, the client should keep using the original URL in the future.
meaning: It is somewhere else, but only for now.

title: 304 — Not Modified
content: The resource has not changed since the client last asked for it, so no body is sent. The client uses its cached copy.
meaning: Nothing changed, use what you already have.

title: 400 — Bad Request
content: The server cannot process the request because it is malformed: invalid syntax, broken JSON, or parameters that make no sense.
meaning: The request is malformed and cannot be read.

title: 401 — Unauthorized
content: Authentication is missing or the credentials are invalid. The name is misleading: this is about identity, not permissions.
meaning: I do not know who you are, identify yourself first.

title: 403 — Forbidden
content: The server understood the request and knows who you are, but you are not allowed to access this resource. Authenticating again will not help.
meaning: I know who you are, but you cannot come in.

title: 404 — Not Found
content: The server could not find the requested resource. It does not say whether it never existed or was deleted, only that there is nothing at that URL.
meaning: There is nothing here.

title: 418 — I'm a teapot
content: An April Fools joke from 1998 that stuck around in the standard. The teapot refuses to brew coffee. Plenty of servers implement it for fun.
meaning: I am a teapot, I do not brew coffee.

title: 429 — Too Many Requests
content: The client sent too many requests in too little time and hit the rate limit. The response usually carries a Retry-After header.
meaning: Slow down, you sent too many requests.

title: 500 — Internal Server Error
content: Something broke on the server side and there is no more specific response available. This is the generic error when the code blew up.
meaning: Something broke on the server side.

title: 501 — Not Implemented
content: The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request. For example, an HTTP method it does not recognize.
meaning: This is not implemented yet.

title: 502 — Bad Gateway
content: The server was acting as a proxy or gateway and got an invalid response from the upstream server. The problem is further back in the chain.
meaning: The server behind me sent back garbage.

title: 503 — Service Unavailable
content: The server cannot handle the request right now: it is down for maintenance or overloaded. Usually temporary.
meaning: I am not available right now.

title: 504 — Gateway Timeout
content: The server was acting as a proxy and waited too long for a response from the upstream server without getting one. Time ran out.
meaning: The server behind me took too long to answer.
